items.weakness_text: One thing that is not immediately clear to me is the utility of the model presented in section 5. It seems like the best procedure would be: * Search over hyperparameters at small scale (e.g. 100M). * Match parameters at larger scale. * Carry out partial training runs at large scale. * Use the partial training runs to select the best run and finish it. It seems to me that even with the model, one may have to run many training runs at the largest scale in order to obtain the normalization factor, aka the finalized loss.
items.ac_evidence: Reviewer J2cjs concerns: The concerns raised were addressed in the rebuttal, and Reviewer J2cj expressed satisfaction with the authors response.

items.weakness_text: The results are done with a fixed (but certainly standard) way of pretraining, i.e., single epoch, AdamW, moderate dataset sizes ("TPP"). The conclusions might not hold or look different for setups with much longer training, data curriculums or optimizers and schedules. Especially longer training (higher "TPP") would be relevant (is there a point where i breaks down?) and extrapolations beyond just training loss.

Minor: Celerity uses a much more refined datamix than just Slimpajama, which makes some comparison (e.g. to BTLM) somewhat hard. But that is discussed (and represents a general improvement of pretraining strategies including data+optimization).
the paper is extremely dense, with lots of notation and terms that make it daunting and complex to grasp for new readers. I think this presentation can be improved.
items.ac_evidence: The concerns regarding readability were addressed by the authors through proposed substantial presentation improvements, including the addition of an intuitive overview in Section 2, a table of symbols, expanded Key Takeaways, and a rewritten biasvariance tradeoff explanation.

items.weakness_text: the authors have not published the code or any of the models as far as I can tell. Since the exact setup is quite unique (e.g., CompleteP), releasing those artifacts would be crucial in enabling better study of the entirety of methods that are included in this line of work.
items.ac_evidence: Regarding the availability of resources, the authors committed to releasing the code (CompleteP) and to seeking approval to release models trained with the Celerity recipe, as well as other artifacts such as loss curve data from the ablation studies.
